name: Partial-order ranking (Hasse diagrams, exact rank probabilities)
title: Which stress-test differences do payouts actually follow?
field: network science and environmental chemistry (multi-indicator ranking without weights)
what: Orders firms only when one is worse on every stress indicator, then counts every full ranking consistent with that partial order.
grade: well established (exact combinatorics; small applied literature)
pick_line: Noise-aware dominance: order firms only when worse beyond projection noise on every indicator, then recompute rank probabilities.
data: Public filings (Fed DFAST/CCAR results 2013–2025, FR Y-9C payouts, SCB); descriptive only
one: 55% of firm pairs have no weight-free stress order; payouts follow pre-tax income there, not loan losses.

picture.la: Usual tool: one composite stress score forces a full order
picture.lb: Hasse diagram, 2024: 53% of pairs have no order

findings.h: Where one firm is worse on all three, it pays out less 72% of the time.
findings.t: Across 13 severely adverse exercises (2013–2025, 360 firm-years), 2,203 within-year pairs are ordered by dominance (worse CET1 drawdown, worse pre-tax income and higher loan-loss rate together). In 71.5% of them the more-stressed firm had the lower Y-9C payout/RWA that calendar year (within-year shuffle null mean 50.0%, 95th percentile 54.7%, p = 0.0002, 4,999 shuffles); next-year payouts 65.5% (p = 0.0002).
findings.note: Every positive-weight composite agrees on these pairs, so this number is the part of the stress–payout link that does not depend on weights. Payouts in calendar year Y partly precede that year's results; association only.

chart.title: Share where the more-stressed firm paid less (dominance pairs)

findings.h: In trade-off pairs, payouts follow pre-tax income and go against loan losses.
findings.t: 55% of pairs per year on average (40–65%) are trade-offs: each firm is worse on something. There, the firm with worse SA pre-tax income paid less in 63.9% of 2,814 pairs (two-sided p = 0.0005); the firm with the higher loan-loss rate paid less in only 40.9% (p = 0.001, i.e. it paid more); drawdown 53.1% (p = 0.19). The equal-weight composite averages these to 55.2%.
findings.note: Computed with a within-year payout shuffle (1,999). Holm over the five orderings keeps pre-tax income, loan losses, equal-weight and OLS significant. The in-sample OLS composite (61.5%) uses payouts to choose its weights, so it is optimistic. No composite can show the sign reversal: it is hidden inside the weights.

chart.la: Agreement by ordering (dominance vs trade-off pairs)
chart.lb: 2024 rank probabilities (orange) vs the composite (teal dots)

findings.h: When the stress path and the SCB disagree, payouts follow the path.
findings.t: 2021–2025: in 175 pairs where one firm is worse on the whole stress path but its SCB is not higher (123 of them with both firms at the 2.5% floor), the path-worse firm paid less in 78.9% (shuffle p = 0.001). Ordering by SCB alone gets 56.8% of 1,481 pairs (p = 0.024); path dominance 71.9% of 834 (p = 0.001).
findings.note: Consistent with the 11-14 IDR finding (SCB had no skill). The SCB floor hides differences that payouts still track. SCB and later payouts are linked by construction after 2020 (standardized capital actions); read descriptively.

findings.h: Dominance relations are stable: 74% persist, 2% reverse.
findings.t: For firms in consecutive tests, 1,115 of 1,553 dominance relations persist (mean share 0.74), 409 dissolve into trade-offs and 29 (1.9%) reverse. Payout-rank Kendall τ averages 0.63 and falls after 2020 (0.40–0.69 in 2020–2025 pairs vs 0.53–0.84 before).
findings.note: Descriptive; no null. The stable core of the stress ordering is the part payouts track (finding 1).

findings.h: As a predictor it loses to OLS, ARDL and SARIMAX.
findings.t: Walk-forward 2015–2025 (fits use earlier years only), Spearman of predicted vs realized payout/RWA: poset expected rank 0.36, pooled OLS on the 3 stress variables 0.46, pooled ARDL(1,0) with last year's payout 0.67, per-firm SARIMAX(1,0,0)+exog 0.65 (last payout where < 8 years).
findings.note: Pre-stated bar (within 0.05 of OLS with no fitted weights) failed. Payout persistence dominates any stress ranking. The method is for description, not forecasting.
